builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: From Twisted Facts to Rogue Agents: Can LLMs Reliably Detect Multi-Dimensional Hallucinations?
summary: Replaces ad hoc or narrow hallucination checks with a bilingual benchmark spanning factual text and agent-trajectory faithfulness errors with fine-grained annotations. Costs are limited to evaluation compute and annotation access, but adopting it requires maintaining benchmark infrastructure rather than deploying a detection method. The benchmark itself does not solve hallucination detection and may not transfer to domain-specific production failure modes.
rationale: The reader needs production detection capability, but this is an evaluation benchmark that diagnoses LLM limitations rather than providing a deployable detection mechanism for constrained infrastructure.

claims.statement: Replaces ad hoc or narrow hallucination checks with a bilingual benchmark spanning factual text and agent-trajectory faithfulness errors with fine-grained annotations. Costs are limited to evaluation compute and annotation access, but adopting it requires maintaining benchmark infrastructure rather than deploying a detection method. The benchmark itself does not solve hallucination detection and may not transfer to domain-specific production failure modes.

Experiments on fourteen LLMs reveal basic sample-level detection ability but persistent difficulty with fine-grained localization, correction, and agent hallucination detection; thinking, web search, and supervised fine-tuning each offer only partial improvements.
